description: CASI seeks to spark interest in and facilitate research about AI safety and alignment.

We focus on how you can choose your career to have the *greatest* impact whether by focusing on alleviating global poverty, trying to prevent future pandemics, trying to prevent nuclear war, and lots more. Every semester we run a seminar that outlines all of the areas in which you can have the most impact with your career. The seminar is a bit of a time commitment, taking 3-4 hours per week for eight weeks. There will be weekly meetings and reading assignments. Food will be provided at no cost to you. name: 180 Degrees Consulting CMU Branch
description: 180 Degrees Consulting is the world's largest consultancy for nonprofits and socially focused organizations. Our mission is to ensure that non-profits and social enterprises committed to education, health, and poverty alleviation can reach their full potential by meeting their demand for very affordable, high-quality strategic and operational assistance, and in so doing developing the next generation of social impact leaders.

name: AB Tech
description: The Activities Board Technical Committee, commonly known as AB Tech, is the student organization charged with handling the technical production of Carnegie Mellon-sponsored events, including all events organized by the Activities Board. AB Tech provides high-quality, professional-grade entertainment production services, including sound reinforcement, lighting design, and event management at heavily subsidized rates to the Carnegie Mellon University community. name: AC Mellon Men's Soccer Team
description: Our ambition is to foster a fun competitive culture and win at the highest soccer club levels. We find success in our commitment to the club and our positive culture.

name: ACM@CMU
description: The mission of this organization is to be the leading premier organization for computing professionals at Carnegie Mellon. We are dedicated to promoting interdisciplinary computing and enabling professional development on campus.

name: Activities Board
description: To provide quality programming for the CMU student body!

name: acts2fellowship
description: Acts2Fellowship (A2F) is a Christian fellowship for students at CMU. We're a group of students and mentors who love Jesus. We do life together, go on trips, study together, serve the community and above all, investigate the biggest questions of life and grow in our faith.

name: Adam Smith Society
description: The Adam Smith Society is a community of business school students and alumni who believe that business, entrepreneurship, and commerce are wellsprings that keep this country vibrant, creative, prosperous, and free. Our members are dedicated to exploring the links among the economy, government, and society through rigorous debate and discussion. The Society aims to build an influential network of future business leaders dedicated to preserving and strengthening the free-market economic system. name: Alpha Kappa Psi Professional Business Fraternity
description: Alpha Kappa Psi is the nation's oldest and largest co-ed professional fraternity open to all majors and interests. Here at Carnegie Mellon, the Omega Psi chapter has established itself as a leading student organization, consistently attracting the best and brightest minds on campus.

name: Alpha Omega Campus Ministry
description: Alpha Omega is a campus ministry in the great city of Pittsburgh helping students to know more about God and fall in love with Him. We are a community of believers committed to Jesus and his ways and our greatest desire is to help others to know Him!

name: Alpha Phi Omega
description: To develop the chapter as an essential part of the CMU and Scouting communities, make diversity and inclusion a priority in our organization, and to best serve Pittsburgh and beyond.

name: Alpine Racing & Freestyle Team
description: Ski Team promotes the sports of ski racing, freestyle skiing and snowboarding on campus. Ski Team provides an opportunity for students who enjoy these sports to compete in the Allegheny Collegiate Ski and Snowboard Conference, a division of the United States Collegiate Ski and Snowboard Association. Ski Team provides resources and support for all competitors to expand their skills and have a safe and enjoyable race experience.

name: American Association for Aerosol Research
description: The American Association for Aerosol Research (AAAR) describes itself as “a nonprofit professional organization for scientists and engineers who wish to promote and communicate technical advances in the field of aerosol research.” The Carnegie Mellon University student chapter of AAAR provides a link between students at CMU and the larger AAAR community. name: American Indigenous Science and Engineering Society
description: Chapters are formed to advance the mission of American Indigenous Science and Engineering Society (AISES) at colleges and universities with Indigenous students in attendance and/or official support services for these students. The objective is to support the success of Native American, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander students in their intellectual, academic, social, and professional pursuits in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) and related disciplines.

name: American Institute of Architecture Students
description: The mission of The American Institute of Architecture Students shall be to promote excellence in architectural education, training, and practice; to foster an appreciation of architecture and related disciplines; to enrich communities in a spirit of collaboration; and to organize students and combine their efforts to advance the art and science of architecture.

name: American Society of Civil Engineers
description: To empower our members by providing a diverse and inclusive support system which includes students, alumni, faculty, and industry professionals. We provide social, academic, and professional support as well as opportunities to hear from different leading civil and environmental engineering companies about the work that they are doing to shape our future.

name: American Society of Mechanical Engineers
description: ASME's mission is to serve the Carnegie Mellon and Pittsburgh Communities by advancing and applying engineering knowledge for improving the quality of life. We also seek to exemplify the excitement of Engineering.

name: Apex
description: Apex began in 2012 when a group of friends living in the Rez on Fifth had the crazy idea of starting a buggy team. Now in its second decade, Apex remains dedicated to the principles that motivated its formation: teamwork, passion, innovation, and excitement. As an open source team, Apex aims to challenge the field of buggy by not living up to the status quo set by other organizations. We want to see the sport succeed through collaboration within the buggy community! Apex is a team of pushers, drivers, and mechanics. name: Architectural Crafts Collective
description: To create a platform for students interested in architecture and design to collaborate and expand their knowledge on fabrication, design, and creative skills with an emphasis on traditional crafts and techniques

name: Arm Wrestling Club
description: AWC intends to teach others about the techniques of safe arm wrestling and promote strength/exercise across campus. Members will learn the vital importance of being stronger. AWC embraces a long standing motto: “Make your way up the food chain” to symbolize one’s journey in becoming the strongest version of themselves.

name: Artist Alley Club
description: In anime and comic conventions, there is a section for independent artists to sell their work. This is called the "artist alley". Artist Alley Club is a community of artists dedicated to helping each other with activities related to participating in artist alley, like creating original and fan art and printing and making merchandise of it. We also act as a community for artists who are generally part of the artist alley subculture: fan-artists and people who make cartoon-, video game-, or anime-inspired art.

name: Asian Students Association
description: The Asian Students Association seeks to empower and connect the Asian American and Pacific Islander community at Carnegie Mellon University.

name: Association of Latino Professionals For America
description: The purpose of this organization is to create a community here at Carnegie Mellon University where Latino students are empowered to contribute to one another's growth, development, and successes, both personally while they are here on campus and professionally as they look to step into the workforce.

name: Astronomy Club
description: Founded in 1967, we are a diverse group of Carnegie Mellon undergrads, graduate students, and community members who are astronomy and space enthusiasts. We meet throughout the fall and spring semesters, discuss astronomy, take trips to observatories and museums, and go observing whenever we get the chance (admittedly infrequent in cloudy Pittsburgh).

name: Awareness of Roots in Chinese Culture
description: Awareness of Roots in Chinese Culture (ARCC) is a CMU organisation which serves to promote Chinese culture on campus. Our goal is to increase awareness of Chinese culture on the CMU campus by sponsoring large open events, such as the Mid-Autumn Festival, Chinese New Year and Dumpling Nights, along with organizing annual cultural performances involving traditional dance, martial arts, and musical performances. We hope that you will join us at our events and learn more about Chinese culture!

name: Badminton Club
description: The goal of this organization is to cultivate an increased interest in badminton at CMU through providing badminton enthusiasts a safe community to develop their skills. With opportunities to train weekly and compete in tournaments, Badminton Club aims to foster a motivating and competitive atmosphere for its members, encouraging every athlete to continue their journey with badminton.

name: Ballroom Dance Club
description: The CMU Ballroom Dance Club's goal is to create a setting for learning social and competitive ballroom dancing in a fun and relaxed environment. Our club's members range from those with two left feet (and sometimes more) to veteran dancers with years of experience. We welcome anyone interested in learning and having fun, including Pittsburgh area undergraduate students, graduate students, and professionals. If you don't have a partner, no worries! We welcome singles and couples.

name: Bangladeshi Student Organization
description: The Bangladeshi Student Organization (BSO) at Carnegie Mellon University aims to provide a home for students and faculty of Bengali descent. Our mission is to foster a supportive environment where Bengali students can celebrate and stay connected to their cultural heritage. We are equally committed to building an inclusive community that welcomes all CMU students who are interested in learning about Bangladeshi culture, traditions, and perspectives.

name: BAPS Campus Fellowship (BCF)
description: BAPS Campus Fellowship (BCF) at Carnegie Mellon University exists to unite students through the exploration of the Swaminarayan Hindu tradition. Our mission is to provide meaningful opportunities for spiritual growth, cultural understanding, and community service while fostering dialogue and fellowship that help students balance academic life with personal values and a commitment to serving others.

name: Be The Match
description: Our goal is to raise awareness and money for the Be The Match charity. This charity gets people on a registry for donating their hematopoietic stem cells, which can save lives through transplants to those with blood cancer and other diseases.

name: Bhakti Yoga Club
description: To create a welcoming and inclusive community space grounded in the principles of bhakti yoga, the yoga of devotion and loving service. We aim to help students relieve stress through various meditation techniques, including music meditation, while offering opportunities for spiritual growth, connection, and cultural exchange.

name: Bhangra in the Burgh
description: Bhangra in the Burgh's mission is to promote Indian and more specifically Punjabi culture within the Pittsburgh community through our annual premier dance competition. We also hope to give back to the Pittsburgh community by donating all proceeds to a charity of our choice every year.

name: Big Straw Magazine
description: The Asian-interest publication that started over a cup of bubble tea. Big Straw is a student-run Asian-interest publication that celebrates the creative talent and intellectual depth of the Asian and Asian American community at Carnegie Mellon University by providing students with an outlet for artistic expression, cultural identity, and thought. Big Straw was founded with the goal to cultivate and spread ideas relevant to Asians and Asian Americans.

name: Biomedical Engineering Society, Carnegie Mellon Chapter
description: The objective of this chapter shall be to promote the profession of Biomedical Engineering through organized study, research, social, and industry immersed activities. These activities will work to further the dissemination of information on the topic and profession of biomedical engineering, as well as its interaction with the other science disciplines. The chapter shall promote membership in the BMES by facilitating community within the student body and faculty through the ideas, purposes and objectives of BMES.

name: Birding@CMU
description: We hope to create a love for birds and conservation at CMU and beyond.

name: Block Center for Technology and Society
description: Block Center is a campus wide research center that serve the entire CMU campus/community to explore the intersections of technological innovation, public policy, and society.

name: Carnegie Involvement Association
description: Founded in 1970, CIA was the first independent (non-Greek) organization to win Sweepstakes, or Buggy. Open to all members of the student body, CIA's objective is to strike the right balance between performing well and having fun.

name: Carnegie Mellon ACEing Autism
description: A. The mission of CMU ACEing Autism is to build a community of volunteers, families, athletes, coaches and participants that is empowered by a shared mission of inclusion and acceptance of the neurodivergent community. In addition, CMU ACEing Autism aims to make tennis accessible to individuals with intellectual and/or physical disabilities to support their growth and development both socially and physical well-being. B. All activities and functions of the organization must be legal under University, local, state, and federal laws.

name: Carnegie Mellon Artificial Intelligence Club
description: The Carnegie Mellon Artificial Intelligence Club (CMUAI) is committed to fostering a dynamic community for AI enthusiasts. Through seminars, hackathons, and collaborations, we aim to amplify understanding, promote its application in daily life, and ensure CMU remains at the AI forefront.

name: Carnegie Mellon Business Association
description: The mission of CMBA is to provide students with the opportunity to learn about and engage with various aspects of the business world. From industry panels to LinkedIn workshops, we aim to help our peers hone skills applicable to interviewing, searching for jobs, and presenting well. CMBA also hosts three industry programs where participants learn about their respective field through a prepared curriculum, interactive discussions, and internal competitions.

name: Carnegie Mellon Club XC
description: To provide a space for a team and community for passionate endurance runners to compete interscholasitically and train together.

name: Carnegie Mellon College Progressives
description: The CMCP’s mission is to build an educational foundation for leftist theory and practice on CMU’s campus. We advocate for and help organize workers on and off campus, create a space to study and discuss relevant leftist literature, and analyze local politics through a socialist lens; with a focus on class, race, and LGBTQ+ issues, imperialism and colonialism, the labor movement, and more.

name: Carnegie Mellon College Republicans
description: The purpose of the Carnegie Mellon College Republicans is to raise awareness for Republican and conservative values within Carnegie Mellon University. Our overall objective is to promote open discourse and critical thinking regarding politics by providing a platform which allows insight into conservative values through structured discussion.

name: Carnegie Mellon Colombian Student Organization
description: Promoting Colombian heritage and providing resources for student success and community involvement.

name: Carnegie Mellon Data Science Club
description: The purpose of this organization is to serve as a platform for CMU students to pursue their interests in data science in a setting that is supportive, collaborative, and competitive.

name: Carnegie Mellon Racing
description: As an organization, we aim to be at the forefront of electric vehicle racecar technology. We provide students with opportunities for technical and management experience on a large engineering project. We strive to cultivate excellent engineers, leaders, and problem solvers. Our team is accessible to all people of different experience levels, backgrounds, and areas of study.

name: Carnegie Mellon University Club Squash
description: Carnegie Mellon University club squash is a co-ed, all-levels team for anyone interested in playing squash. As a student-run club, we host 3-4 optional practices per week and occasional squash workshops for each level. We also compete against different club squash teams outside of Carnegie Mellon University and attend tournaments including the National Collegiate Club Team Championships hosted by the college squash association.

name: Carnegie Mellon University Club Swimming
description: CMU Club swimming is a fun way to keep in shape and be part of a great group on campus. We have practices 3 times per week, attend 2-4 meets per semester against other schools, and have various social events. We are open to people of all swimming levels, ranging from those that just want to stay shape to those that want to be competitive at meets. Practices are Tuesdays 7-9pm, Wednesdays 9-11pm, and Sundays 4-5:30pm. Practices are optional and you can show up or leave whenever convenient. We will provide a swim set and equipment to use during practice. INSTAGRAM: @cmuclubswimming

name: Carnegie Mellon University Cricket Club
description: The CMU Cricket club is for all cricket lovers. We promote the sport for one and all, be it current students, alumni, faculty to enjoy and learn the game of cricket at CMU. The mission of the club is not just to promote the sport itself, but also build future leaders and develop team work through this sport.

name: Carnegie Mellon University Figure Skating Club
description: To promote figure skating at CMU and build a community of figure skaters

name: Carnegie Mellon University Global Medical Brigades
description: CMU GMB is a chapter of the national organization Global Brigades. Global Brigades is a global health and sustainable development organization that aims to empower rural communities in Guatemala, Panama, Honduras, and Ghana through student brigades. CMU GMB's mission is to aid in this initiative by providing access to medical care and creating sustainable infrastructures in underserved communities abroad. name: Carnegie Mellon University Math Club
description: The purpose of CMUMC shall be to promote the mathematical growth of individuals within CMU with a focus on the undergraduate experience. We aim to hold social and informational events that will promote the holistic and professional goals of students interested in mathematics.

name: Carnegie Mellon University Model United Nations
description: The purpose of the Carnegie Mellon University Model United Nations Team is to encourage and promote diplomacy, dialogue, and understanding of different cultures and ideas through the provision of academic and social events relevant to international cooperation, understanding, and education

name: Carnegie Mellon University Poker Club
description: The Undergraduate Poker Club strives to be a hub for the poker community at Carnegie Mellon University to meet, learn, and play. We aim to engage all manner of poker players with a wide array of events that include everything from charity tournaments and interactive workshops to guest speakers and networking opportunities. Outside of CMU, we seek to build lasting connections with trading firms and other companies that are interested in students with the strategic and analytical skills developed through poker.

name: Carnegie Mellon Young Americans for Liberty
Carnegie Strategy Group

We provide CMU students with applied practice experience with real-world client (a) campaigns and (b) startups facing regulatory hurdles across the US.

name: Carnegie Tech Radio Club
description: The radio club is an organization of people interested in all the activities amateur radio has to offer. Our membership consists of undergraduates, graduate students, faculty, and staff of the CMU community. Among the club members there is a wide variety of interests such as public service events, satellite communications, DXing (talking to other amateurs around the world), computers and networks, amateur television, and emergency drills. name: Catholic Newman Club
description: The Catholic Newman Club is a social, religious, and service organization for students, staff, and faculty who are Catholic or otherwise interested in the faith.

name: Center for Leadership Studies
description: The Center for Leadership Studies at Carnegie Mellon University helps students grow as effective and ethical leaders by offering courses, workshops, coaching, and mentoring that build skills such as vision, communication, reflection, and decision-making.

name: Center for Shared Prosperity (CSP)
description: The Center for Shared Prosperity helps CMU and the Pittsburgh community work together on projects that lower barriers to equity and prosperity. With compassion, collaboration and curiosity we engage with our neighbors to achieve shared prosperity in our region.

description: The Central Church of Pittsburgh Korean Ministry aims to promote cultural awareness and appreciation among students by organizing a Christian Ministry. This mission seeks to foster unity, celebrate diversity, and provide an opportunity for students to learn about the Bible and foster spiritual growth. description: Central Church exists to make and mature disciples of Jesus Christ, so that the Gospel of Jesus Christ is the foundational principle through which we live in our homes, in our church, in our work, and in the city of Pittsburgh.

name: Chabad of CMU
description: The purpose of Chabad of CMU is to promote positive Jewish activities and views within the university community. Chabad of CMU is also a home away from home for Jews at Carnegie Mellon University. Through social, educational and spiritual programming, Chabad helps strengthen their Jewish awareness, pride, and identity, helping them establish a life-long, personal connection to Judaism.

name: Chess Club
description: Our mission is to unite the chess community at CMU and introduce new players to the game. We aim to foster a welcoming environment for chess enthusiasts of all levels and provide resources for players to improve their skills.

name: Chinese Student Association
description: Chinese Student Association's primary mission is to provide Chinese undergraduate students with a homely community and help them adjust to life here at Carnegie Mellon University. CSA also promotes Chinese culture and maintains open social platforms for all students. description: The mission of CSSA is bring everyone together by holding external and internal events that create opportunities for Chinese students and scholars as well as students from other country to meet each other and establish mutual-beneficial relationships. Our organization aims to provide a second home for international students from China and familiarize Chinese students with CMU as well as the Pittsburgh community. description: To build a supportive community where Tepper students grow in faith, develop as values-driven leaders, and apply virtuous principles to create lasting impact in business and society

description: The mission of the club is to facilitate gatherings of students who are interested in learning about, experiencing, and enjoying Jesus Christ and the Bible.

name: Circle K
description: Circle K International is committed to developing leaders by offering unique service, leadership, and fellowship opportunities that allow members to positively impact communities around the world and help others feel like they have a place where they belong.

name: Club Baseball
description: Our mission is to field a competitive baseball team that works hard and plays their absolute best every time we take the field. We also want to make sure all of our players have fun while doing so as we are not only a team, but a family. We wish to respect the game through hard work and integrity while trying to be successful and an overall winning ball club.

name: CMQ+
description: CMQ+ (formerly Allies Grad) serves LGBTQIA+ graduate students at Carnegie Mellon University, though staff and/or allies are always welcome at our events. The + denotes allies, non-identifying, HIV+ and others. We are open to interpretation and an avowal of both our inclusivity and focus on queer identifying people at CMU. We aim to help create an affirming and rewarding social and intellectual environment for this community, as well as tangible support for graduate students at Carnegie Mellon of all gender identities and sexual orientations. name: CMU Abhinaya
description: Our members are trained in Kuchipudi, Bharatanatyam, Odissi and Mohiniattam, among other styles of dance. We are united by a collective passion to convey stories, experiences and emotions through movement. CMU Abhinaya is a space to connect with one's Indian heritage, build community and practice physical and mental well-being. We perform at several events during the school year including Diwali, Holi and Dancer's Symposium. Our vision for this year is to expand our presence on campus and be a part of bigger communities and events.

name: CMU Bhangra
description: The purpose of Carnegie Mellon University Bhangra (CMU Bhangra) is to provide an opportunity and instruction for aspiring dancers, and to represent CMU in a positive light in an international community through cultural expression.

name: CMU Blockchain Group
description: Carnegie Mellon Blockchain is focused on developing and understanding the decentralized future and being the hub of all crypto and blockchain activity on Carnegie Mellon's campus.

name: CMU Board Game Club
description: CMU Board Game Club -- We play games. We provide a venue for the practice of board-, card-, and other forms of social tabletop games. We meet every Saturday in the Foster Dining room on the 2nd floor of the UC, directly above Entropy (backup Zoom link: https://cmu.zoom.us/j/93450695745?pwd=L25TUHhVK2RrSFlDbWh5T2NScUplQT09). We begin at 1:00 pm. Gaming lasts until everyone goes home. To join our mailing list, sign up here: https://lists.andrew.cmu.edu/mailman/listinfo/board-game-club

name: CMU Business Technology Group
description: Business Technology Group is an organization at Carnegie Mellon University that focuses on providing undergraduates and graduate students that are interested in business and technology with real-world projects, a strong understanding of potential career paths, and offer them opportunities to gain hands-on experience in their areas of interest. BTG specializes in applied technology that improves work, play, and education in Pittsburgh.

name: CMU ChemE Car
description: The students of the ChemE Car, a student project team, maintain a goal of designing, building, and testing a small-scale automobile that is powered and controlled by chemical means to compete in regional and national competitions sponsored by AIChE. All majors are welcome!

name: CMU ChemE Cube
description: The ChemE Cube team aims to design, build, and test a 1 cubic foot plant that produces a desired product based on an annual problem statement provided by the RAPID Manufacturing Institute. The team competes at the annual competition held during the AIChE Student Conference through a head-to-head duel and creation of an ad, poster, and pitch presented to judges during the competition.

name: CMU Cubing Club
description: The organization aims to create a welcoming environment focused on promoting twisty puzzles, Rubik’s cubes, and speedcubing activities.

name: CMU Cyphers
description: The main purpose of the CMU Cypher Club (hitherto referred to as CMU Cyphers) is to provide a comfortable, low-commitment environment for people to share their talents at rapping and hear the work of others. It will also give people an opportunity to give and receive feedback, as well as practice, to improve their own abilities. This club is open to all members of the university community. All activities and functions of the organization must be legal under University, local, state, and federal laws.

name: CMU Debate
description: CMU debate aims to foster a community of individuals interested in speech and rhetoric and promote the value of public speaking to the greater CMU community.

name: CMU Esports
description: CMU Esports is a student organization at Carnegie Mellon University that strives to offer both a competitive and casual gaming scene that is accessible to all students. We recruit and train highly competitive collegiate teams for all popular games while hosting gaming events of all shapes and sizes on campus for all students.

name: CMU Explorers Club
description: We are a student run organization dedicated to bringing together people with an interest in the outdoors since 1959. We venture into the wilderness through organized activities such as rock and ice climbing, mountaineering, caving, hiking, backpacking, flat and white water boating, sailing, skydiving, mountain biking, scuba diving, and more.

name: cmu filmmakers
description: At CMU Filmmakers, we bring together aspiring storytellers to learn the art of filmmaking through hands-on experience. Our mission is to offer fun workshops where students can learn about Movie/TV pitching, writing and production from industry professionals.

name: CMU Fishing Club
description: The CMU fishing club's mission is to promote the sport and prosperity of fishing at CMU. This is through educational sessions with older members on proper and sustainable fishing practices and fishing outings. The CMU fishing club aims to make it easy and convenient for students to partake in humane and ethical fishing.

name: CMU Global
description: To promote, support and create opportunities and student led initiatives for students to connect and network with their peers on all CMU campuses across the globe.

name: CMU Global Buddies
description: CMU Global Buddies fosters friendship, cultural exchange, and community between international exchange students and domestic students at Carnegie Mellon University. To support these connections, CGB pairs incoming exchange students with current CMU Pittsburgh students based on shared interests or goals, forming buddy groups. CGB also organizes on and off campus events where buddy groups can meet, socialize, and build lasting relationships.

name: CMU Green Practices
description: We work to advance operational sustainability efforts across all aspect of university support services and offer programming to foster a campus culture of environmental sustainability.

name: CMU Hindu YUVA
description: The mission of the CMU Hindu YUVA organization is to bring together both Hindu and non-Hindu students to raise awareness about what Hinduism is. As one of the largest and oldest religions in the world, we believe it is necessary that there be an organization on campus to represent the interests of the Hindu community present here.

name: CMU HOX Business Fraternity
description: Eta Omega Chi(HOX) aims to provide professional developments and connections to its members and build a tunnel for mutually beneficial relationships between the graduated alumni and current students for professional purposes.

name: CMU Jiya
description: CMU Jiya is Carnegie Mellon's premier award-winning all-girls competitive Bollywood fusion team, combining a variety of different dance styles from western styles like hip-hop and contemporary, to Indian classical and fold dances. Our dancers aim to exhibit our passion for dance and showcase their love for Indian culture. The troupe's members excel at a variety of dance styles and many have been dancing since childhood, but some have just begun dancing as recently as when they joined Jiya. description: OM is an independent non-sectarian forum for the education and promotion of the Indian cultural and spiritual heritage. Students, faculty, and all other members of the Carnegie Mellon community are welcome to join. OM provides cultural and spiritual assistance to Hindus, Jains, Sikhs, and other cultures, backgrounds and religions of Indian origin. name: CMU Pasage
description: To provide networking and creative opportunities to college students and connect them with industry work before graduation.

name: CMU Pickleball
description: The mission of this club is to connect people who play or are interested in playing pickleball at CMU as well as introduce the game to new players. Our activities include but are not limited to: pickleball lessons, organized singles and doubles match play, and tournaments. This club will also provide equipment for players who need it.

name: CMU Pool Club
description: Our mission is to promote the sport of pool at the collegiate level and bolster the existing community of pool enthusiasts. We are also resurging our pool team such that players' interest in competing at a high level becomes feasible.

name: CMU Powerlifting
description: The goal of this club is to provide both avid and new lifters a safe community to grow stronger together at CMU. Through group practices, meets, and clinics, CMU Powerlifting promises to foster an uplifting and supportive atmosphere for all members to become the best lifters they can be. All activities and functions of the organization must be legal under University, local, state, and federal laws.

name: CMU Private Equity & Venture Capital Club
description: The Club aims to strengthen the private equity and venture capital ecosystem at Carnegie Mellon University by promoting collaboration, education, and professional development for students and alumni. We connect private market firms with students, offer educational resources, and provide access to industry experts. Furthermore, we encourage interdisciplinary engagement across various schools to build a vibrant network of private investment enthusiasts.

name: CMU Raasta
description: CMU Raasta is a dance team committed to promoting Indian culture across campus. Through the West Indian folk dance garba-raas, we aim to spread awareness of our traditions. By performing on and off campus at dance competitions throughout the nation, we wish to exhibit the talent and diversity of Carnegie Mellon students.

name: CMU Recreational Badminton Club
description: The CMU Recreational Badminton Club strives to offer a free and comfortable environment for players of all levels to engage in badminton recreationally. In addition, the club aims to advocate for badminton and recreational badminton players in the CMU community. The club also will promote an awareness of the sport and foster respect for all other athletes.

name: CMU Red Cross
description: The American Red Cross prevents and alleviates human suffering in the face of emergencies by mobilizing the power of volunteers and the generosity of donors.

name: CMU RPG Association
description: The CMU RPG Association aims to support fans of role-playing games on the Carnegie Mellon University campus.

name: CMU Saans
description: CMU Saans is Carnegie Mellon's premier South Asian a cappella team, coming together to share our passion for music and celebrate South Asian culture. Performing both at on campus showcases as well as in competitions across the country, we hope to continue representing Carnegie Mellon on a national level. We also aim to spread awareness about South Asian culture through the medium of music, while also finding a platform to express our cultural identity.

name: CMU Science Olympiad
description: The purpose of Science Olympiad at Carnegie Mellon University is to inspire interest in the study of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) among youth by organizing and directing Science Olympiad tournaments on campus.

name: CMU Shopno: Bengali Student Association
description: CMU Shopno is an organization that is dedicated to honoring and educating the CMU community on Bengali culture.

name: CMU Special Olympics
description: The Special Olympics strives to create a better world by fostering the acceptance and inclusion of all people: through the power of sports, people with intellectual disabilities discover new strengths and abilities, skills, and success. The Three Rivers Region branch of Special Olympics has hosted its regional competition, the Western Spring Sectional, on the Carnegie Mellon University campus since 2016. This student-run organization aims to bolster student, faculty, and CMU engagement to volunteer for the Western Spring Sectional. We assist Special Olympics' Three Rivers Region in recruiting

name: CMU Sport Taekwondo Club
description: The Carnegie Mellon University Sport Taekwondo Club was formed on behalf of the Carnegie Mellon University community. It is an organization that pursues the tenets of the World Taekwondo Federation (WTF), the international governing body of Olympic-style taekwondo. Thus, we feel that the absence of a World Taekwondo Federation taekwondo club deprives the campus community of complete taekwondo-presence, and we therefore commit ourselves to the exposition of this sport to Carnegie Mellon University.

name: CMU Star Wars
description: To build a community of Star Wars fans across the CMU galaxy.

name: CMU Street Styles
description: CMU Street Styles, est. 2003 as the International Freestylers, is Carnegie Mellon University’s student organization dedicated to teaching and engaging in street dance and hip hop culture. Street Styles strives to bring the knowledge and love of street dance and hip hop culture to as many members of the CMU and broader Pittsburgh dance community as possible. Members of this organization will regularly practice their chosen dance styles, perform for their peers to showcase their progress, and support one another in- and outside of dance.

name: CMU Summit on US-China Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: As a non-profit student organization, our mission is to connect innovators and entrepreneurs world-wide via events including CMU Summit, Demo Day, Global Opportunities Fair, Hack-a-Startup, and more. Our annual summit, this year held between April 23-25, is a high-profile forum that gathers leading entrepreneurs, venture capitalists, and scholars from the US and China to address real-world challenges and discussing opportunities in various technology and business fields, in addition to providing start-ups with communication and recruitment channels. We encourage communications and collaboratio

name: CMU Table Tennis Club
description: Our mission is to grow table tennis at the collegiate level and bolster the existing local table tennis communities. We also strive to be an open gateway to new players while housing a team that can compete at the highest possible level.

name: CMU Tennis Club
description: Our mission is to foster a community for tennis on campus for players of all levels and also provide a more competitive environment for intermediate to advanced level players.

name: CMU Transportation Club
description: The Carnegie Mellon University Transportation Club aims to expose students to transportation-related classes; promote transportation research opportunities; to be a platform for networking and collaboration amongst students, faculty and industry leaders; and to raise awareness of employment opportunities in the transportation industry.

name: CMU Vegan Society
description: Connecting Through Food, Activism, and Social Events

name: CMU Wushu Club
description: The mission of CMU Wushu is to become a supportive place for anyone who is interested in either learning about or practicing wushu. We focus on taolu, which is a performative, non-contact sport.

name: cmuTV
description: cmuTV provides clubs on campus with livestream and recording capabilities! We also maintain a Youtube account with hundreds of videos dating back more than a decade, working with Dancer's Symposium, Lunar Gala, Buggy, and more. To its members cmuTV provides a creative outlet, an opportunity to learn new skills, and a friendly, curious community. To the campus community at large, cmuTV provides essential services including professional video recording and equipment rentals.

name: College Democrats
description: The Carnegie Mellon University chapter of the College Democrats organization dedicated to electing Democrats across the country using the power of the student voice.

name: ColorStack at CMU
description: ColorStack’s mission is to increase the entrance, retention, and success of Black, Latinx, and Native American students in computing through community building, academic support, and professional development.

name: Community & Inclusion
description: Provide the community with information regarding programs and events related to equity, diversity, inclusion and belonging.

name: Computational Biology Society (CBS)
description: The Carnegie Mellon Computational Biology Undergraduate Society (CMU-CBUS) is committed to bringing computational biology majors and students interested in computational biology together in a welcoming and active community through academic and social events. CMU-CBUS will organize events to showcase computational biology research at CMU and beyond, plan socials to foster connections between computational biology students and faculty, and support students in attending computational biology conferences (e.g. ISMB). CMU-CBUS will maintain a close relationship with Carnegie Mellon University's Ray

name: Computer Club
description: Does the thought of: • Finding nifty programming projects to hack on • Getting advice from experts on your own projects • Developing useful services for the CMU community • Deploying your projects in an on-campus, student-run datacenter, alongside KGB, the Tartan, ScottyLabs, and PPP • Trying out the latest technologies in a robust, distributed, production environment • Contributing to free and open source software • Tinkering with Amigas, old Apples, VAXen, DECstations, HP9000s, SPARCs, and others ...get you hyped? Then stop by at one of our meetings. We hold Open Hacking Hours weekly during

name: Computer Graphics & Animation Club
description: The Computer Graphics and Animation (CGA) club is a club for analogue and digital enthusiasts interested in exploring motion-based and physics-based graphics, such as those seen in Disney/Pixar movies and video games today. We hope to foster a learning community for those interested in traditional animation, as well as various 2D and 3D software programs such as Blender and Maya.

name: Consortium for Graduate Student in Management
description: In collaboration with the Consortium since 2001, the Tepper School of Business empowers aspiring leaders from underrepresented ethnic groups by providing a transformative business education and fostering a network of success. We commit to increasing diversity within the business landscape and developing future generations of ethical and impactful leaders.

name: Counterpoint
description: Counterpoint was founded in 2000 by Carolyn Weger as Carnegie Mellon's first all treble voices identifying a cappella group. In 2008, we founded the AcaPittsburgh benefit concert, and we have been holding concerts to benefit local causes and non-profits every year since. We also compete at the International Championship of Collegiate A Cappella (ICCA) annually. In 2023, Counterpoint placed second at the ICCA Central Quarterfinals and moved onto Semifinals in Buffulo, NY.

name: Cru
description: Cru is a community where the gospel captures hearts, transforms lives, and launches men and women into a lifelong adventure with Jesus Christ.

name: Department of Athletics
description: The Carnegie Mellon University Department of Athletics, Physical Education, and Recreation will provide a transformative and inclusive educational experience that nurtures competitiveness, wellness, belonging and resilience, and provides students with a leadership framework to live healthy and impactful lives.

name: Design For America
description: Design For America x CMU is a group of interdisciplinary students who use their unique design, engineering, and social sciences perspectives to confront social issues in innovative ways. As a chapter of national DFA, we use the human centered design process empathize and work with our users we research, ideate, prototype, test and develop solutions. We collaborate in teams of students with diverse backgrounds and interests to develop well-rounded solutions and fuse collaboration, leadership, and creativity. name: Doctors of Carnegie Society
description: The purpose of the Doctors of Carnegie Society is to provide students with information related to the health professions and professional school application process, to increase health awareness, and to be of beneficial service to the Carnegie Mellon University campus community.

name: Economics Club
description: To promote interest in the field of economics and its analytical mode of thought, to engage students' thinking and discussion skills through club dialogue and talks with professors and professionals, to introduce undergraduates to the various branches of the discipline and opportunities on and off campus.

name: Emergency Medical Service
description: The primary purpose of CMU EMS is to provide professional, high quality, timely, reliable and appropriate pre-hospital treatment for medical emergencies within our coverage area. The secondary purpose of the organization is to provide a community for EMS providers at Carnegie Mellon as well as an opportunity for those providers to practice emergency medicine. name: Emerging Leaders
description: A long-standing CMU tradition for first-year students, Emerging Leaders (EL) promotes the development of leadership skills through the lens of community engagement and social action.

name: Filipino Student Association
description: The Filipino Student Association aims to promote and educate people about Filipino culture. We provide a space for students to connect and bond through food, arts & crafts, karaoke, and our overall appreciation of the Philippines. Whether you are from Manila or just want to explore the culture, we hope to serve as an inclusive community for everyone to discover and celebrate what Filipino culture has to offer.

name: Film Club
description: Film Club's mission is to bring cinema to the Carnegie Mellon community in order to create a space for open and constructive dialogue surrounding film and its topics, as well as increase a spirit of film appreciation in the student body. We aim to showcase underrepresented minorities in hopes of exposing audiences to and educating them about experiences and cultures that aren't often shown on the big screen. Foci include women directors, queer directors, cult films, documentaries, and international cinema. Screenings will be followed by moderated discussions.

name: FirstTogether
description: The mission of the FIRST Together program is to enhance the overall success of first generation college students on our campus. Through our intentional and proactive efforts, we offer student-centered opportunities designed to support the academic, professional and campus engagement experiences of our students.

name: Freedom By Design
description: "Freedom by Design”, the AIAS community service program in partnership with the National Council of Architectural Registration Boards (NCARB), uses the talents of architecture students to radically impact the lives of people in their community through modest design and construction solutions. The program embraces efforts to provide both design-build and engagement solutions to address 5 barriers: Physical Educational Environmental Socio-Economic Cultural Freedom by Design├óÔÇ×┬ó (FBD) encourages students to serve their communities by addressing issues with design solutions. name: Fringe
description: Fringe was founded in 1969 by a group of architecture students at Carnegie Mellon University. At the time, it was the first independent student organization to compete in the history of Spring Carnival at CMU. Since then, Fringe has evolved into an all-inclusive group of friends who participate competitively in a variety of campus traditions and co-curricular activities. We are heavily involved in buggy, booth and intramural sports, along with a host of other on-campus events. We are active year-round and have membership from across all of the colleges at CMU.

name: Futurist Club
description: CMU Futurist Club is a space for people of any academic background to gather and share their ideas for what they believe the future should be like. Together we learn frameworks and techniques to practice foresight and speculation and have open minded discussions to better define what your preferred future looks like. Individually, you apply your learnings to your discipline to take steps toward that future.

name: Game Creation Society
description: Game Creation Society (GCS) is a student-run organization at Carnegie Mellon University, dedicated to the development of games. We exist to help members of all skill levels and backgrounds interested in making games learn more about and gain experience in game development. We├óÔé¼Ôäóre fostering a community around the development of student games and provide opportunities to learn, collaborate, get employed, and have fun.

name: Gender Minorities and Women in Physics
description: Gender Minorities & Women in Physics (GWiP) is a student-led organization at Carnegie Mellon University dedicated to fostering an inclusive, supportive, and empowering community for women and gender-minority students in physics or students in all related majors. GWiP seeks to address systemic inequities in STEM by promoting advocacy, mentorship, and professional development, while also building a strong sense of belonging through social and academic engagement. The organization emphasizes intersectionality, recognizing that experiences in physics are shaped by gender, race, ethnicity, sexualit

name: Girls Who Code
description: GWC CMU is an educational outreach non-profit, working in collaboration with the international organization Girls Who Code. GWC CMU is dedicated to closing the gender gap in technology by creating an environment where women in STEM feel empowered and enabling young women with the skill sets to challenge boundaries.

name: Global Business Brigades
description: Global Business Brigades provides business consulting and strategic counseling to support under-resourced micro-enterprises in developing countries. Not only do we address issues such as accounting, operations, and management skills but also we work side-by-side with community members to afford volunteers the opportunity for cultural exchange, micro-finance, and consulting experience. GBB has a tremendous impact on CMU students. The experience of traveling to another country with a great group of friends, getting to know countless hardworking individuals in a country that likely speaks another

name: Google Developer Student Club
description: Google Developer Student Clubs are community groups for college and university students interested in Google developer technologies. Students from all undergraduate or graduate programs with an interest in growing as a developer are welcome. By joining a GDSC, students grow their knowledge in a peer-to-peer learning environment and build solutions for local businesses and their community. Google Developer Student Clubs is a program supported by Google Developers.

name: Graduate Biomedical Engineering Society
description: Building Community within graduate Students of the Biomedical Engineering Department through collaborative projects with student groups in and around the BME Department.

name: Graduate Business Association
description: Mission Statement And Bylaws We, the MBA students of the Carnegie Mellon University Tepper School of Business, establish this Charter and By-Laws for the Carnegie Mellon University Tepper School of Business Graduate Business Association (GBA) Student Government. The GBA is hereby established as a means of representing the interests of the student body of the Carnegie Mellon University business masters programs. Through the establishment of an elected Student Government, it shall provide a platform for the discussion of issues of student concern and act as the instr

name: Graduate Student Assembly
description: The Graduate Student Assembly (GSA) is the branch of student government that represents all graduate students at Carnegie Mellon University. The GSA’s mission is to advocate for and support the diverse needs of all CMU graduate students in their personal, professional, and public lives.

name: Grappling Club
description: The Grappling Club aims to provide students the opportunity to learn and practice grappling-based martial arts, specifically Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Judo, and Wrestling, in a safe setting. Regardless of experience or age, Grappling Club wants to help students to gain and hone their skills for self-defense or for competition, while developing self-discipline and improved mental and physical well-being.

name: Greek Sing
description: Greek Sing aims to stimulate philanthropic & community service efforts for the betterment of the Greek community, Carnegie Mellon campus community, and the Pittsburgh Community. For the 2024 and 2025 years, our partnered charity is Camp Kesem.

name: Habitat for Humanity
description: Habitat for Humanity at Carnegie Mellon seeks to empower volunteer-minded students to build homes, communities, and reason for hope. We strive for a world where everyone has a decent and dignified place to live.

name: Hillel Jewish Students Association
description: To enrich the lives of Jewish students and the CMU community so that they may enrich the Jewish people and the world.

name: Historical European Martial Arts Club
description: Our mission is to bring the sport of HEMA fencing to the CMU community. We aim to teach people the art of fencing in the historical styles of medieval Europe. Compared to arts such as olympic fencing which focus primarily on the sports side of things, we also have a historical aspect to our art which spans centuries and can help to put into perspective why the weapons we practice with developed in the ways that they did. We have frequent group discussions about why certain techniques which were so popular in the manuscripts we reference don't work as well nowadays in sport fencing. These discu

name: Hong Kong Student Association
description: The Hong Kong Student Association at Carnegie Mellon University is an organisation for all those who are interested in Hong Kong culture and its traditions. HKSA is devoted to fostering a stronger Asian community and bringing Hong Kong awareness to campus. As a recognised group in CMU, HKSA strives to bring you fun, meaningful, cultural, and social events throughout the year; while providing opportunities for people who are interested or from Hong Kong to build meaningful relationships.

name: Humanist League
description: The Carnegie Mellon University Humanist League is dedicated to building a community of humanists, who strive to improve the human condition through reason and compassion. We promote discussion over dogma through regular philosophical discussion meetings, and larger speaker events.

name: Ice Hockey
description: Unite players across the university to represent CMU and play hockey in a competitive league.

name: IDEA @ CMU (Inquiry, Discussion, Exploration, and Argument)
description: IDEA @ CMU fosters constructive, open dialogue on controversial, complex, and challenging topics. Rooted in the values of viewpoint diversity, intellectual humility, and open inquiry, the organization provides opportunities for students, faculty, and staff to engage across lines of difference with respect, curiosity, and critical thinking.

name: IEEE CMU Chapter
description: Our mission is to provide a social, technical, and professional community to the ECE student body. We want to help our ECE community gain knowledge, skills and networks that will help them through their academic and professional careers. While CMU IEEE holds many different kinds of events throughout the year, this year we are focusing mostly on social events.

name: Independent Musicians Organization
description: IMO is one of CMU’s most active student-run music orgs, helping students connect with other musicians, form bands with their friends, promote their work, play concerts and plug into the campus and greater Pittsburgh music scene. We host weekly Saturday jam sessions and organize monthly live music both on and off campus, with a mission to unite people through community-oriented programming and live events.

name: Indian Graduate Student Association
description: 1. Enhance cultural connection among Indian Students 2. Help the Indian Cohort with any issues they come up with 3. Organize festive celebrations to spread cultural and social awareness

name: Indonesian Students at CMU
description: To make ISCMU a warm, fun, and enlightening community for Indonesian students at CMU, as well as become a responsive and reliable channel about CMU and Indonesia for external stakeholders in Indonesia, United States, and international communities.

name: INFORMS Student Chapter
description: CMU INFORMS will lead in the developments, dissemination and implementation of knowledge, basic and applied research and technologies in operations research, operations management, business analytics, the management sciences, and related methods of improving operational processes, decision-making, and management. INFORMS will strive to: i. Support efforts to extend, unify and integrate related branches of knowledge and practice ii. Support the free interchange of information relevant to purpose of the group iii. Promote greater use of this knowledge by all organizations public and private iv.

name: Infra Dance Company
description: Hi Infriends! We're Infra, CMU's only intermediate/advanced contemporary dance group. While contemporary is our main focus, our dance styles also include ballet, jazz, tap, and heels. If you love to dance, you should come join us! Whether you are an undergraduate, master's student, or PhD, all students are welcome to join. We're essentially a big family, and are always looking to have new dancers come join us. Our weekly meetings consist of rehearsals & open classes, culminating in an end-of-year showcase during April. Additionally, we perform in Dancers' Symposium each semester and Lunar Gala

name: Inter A Cappella Council
description: Inter A Cappella Council represents the diverse, vibrant a cappella and music community at Carnegie Mellon University. Comprised of members from all 8 of CMU's student-run singing clubs, our goal is to promote and facilitate a cappella music at CMU by providing a platform for individual a cappella organizations to coordinate.

name: Inter-Fellowship Association
description: The purpose of Inter-Fellowship Association (IFA) is to unite Christians (including Christian groups) on campus by organizing campus-wide, inter-fellowship activities, interaction, and service, for the glory of God. We strongly believe that the unity of the Body of Christ at CMU is biblically necessary and our goal is to foster inter-fellowship relations between the many different Christian fellowships and Christian organization. Another way we serve is by acting as a liaison between surrounding churches and other organization, and the CMU Christian community.

name: Interfaith Leadership Development
description: In our diverse world, every career path may lead us to work with people from a variety of different religious, spiritual, and secular worldviews. This Interfaith Leadership Development Program is an opportunity to develop cross-cultural competency and build skills that prepare you to be an effective interfaith leader in your community and particular field of work, while offering many different options that can complement your background, schedule, and interests. To complete this leadership development certificat

name: Interfraternity Council
description: The Interfraternity Council (IFC) exists to advance conditions conducive to the success of its member chapters and to promote the progress of the fraternity experience. With this aim, the IFC actively encourages interfraternalism and collaboration with other fraternity/sorority governing councils and student governance bodies. Maintaining a positive working relationship and partnership with the campus administration, alumni and inter/national headquarters of member chapters is critical toward elevating the role of the IFC.

name: InterVarsity Christian Fellowship
description: In response to God's love, grace, and truth, our mission is to know God and make Him known. In line with this, our vision is to grow in love with God through God's Word, with all of God's people, regardless of ethnicity or culture, for God's purposes in the world.

name: Intervarsity Ignite Black Christian Ministry
description: CMU Ignite is a national Christian InterVarsity organization committed to cultivating personal relationships with Jesus and intentionally embodying His image to inspire others to Christ. As a safe and welcoming space, particularly for the Black and Latine community at CMU, we invite all people, regardless of faith or religious backgrounds, to partake in our pursuit of being God’s hands, feet, and voice on the earth — making disciples of all nations in accordance with His Word.

name: Iranian Student Association
description: The “Iranian Student Associations” strives to Promote the understanding of the social, traditional, and historical aspects of Iranian culture, Provide a source of union and support for the Iranian community, and Help foster friendship among the different cultural groups and the Pittsburgh community in general.

name: Japanese Student Association
description: JSA strives to spread awareness of traditional and modern Japanese culture throughout the university and the greater Pittsburgh area. The organization also aims to connect its members to Japan and Japanese culture, through building partnerships with Japan-related entities. For more information, go to cmujsa.com

name: Jazz Club
description: Our mission is to create an environment and network for musicians to explore and develop their interests in the American art form of jazz. We also aim to share our music with the CMU community, providing live entertainment, a relaxing setting, stress relief, and a community of people to spend time with.

name: Kiltie Band
description: The Kiltie Band is Carnegie Mellon's Marching Band! We have a marching, concert, and pep bands and are open to all experience levels (no auditions!). As one of CMU's oldest student organizations, we pride ourselves on our iconic wacky traditions and making great music to support the athletics department!

name: Korean American Students' Association (KASA)
description: The mission of KASA is to spread awareness of Korean culture and increase appreciation for Korean culture across all groups at Carnegie Mellon University.

name: Korean Graduate Student Association
description: Our organization promotes academic collaboration and social interactions among the Korean graduate students at CMU. We also help Korean CMU graduate students develop their careers by connecting them to alumni, companies, and universities in Korea. Lastly, we provide information to new incoming Korean graduate students about Pittsburgh and CMU to help them get started.

name: Korean Student Association
description: The mission of the Korean Students Association of Carnegie Mellon University shall be to promote Korean culture through cultural, social, political, and community service events. Our activities would range from providing informal social functions to promoting our educational and cultural foundation, which are intrinsically non-political and non-discriminating in nature.

name: Magic@CMU
description: Our mission is to create a friendly and welcoming environment for playing the card game Magic: The Gathering. Join our Discord: https://discord.gg/U3mdyq2qKU

name: MechE Community Engagement Committee
description: Our mission is to create a transformative environment for all members of the MechE community (Students, Faculty and Staff), regardless of status, race, ability, gender, national origin, or other affiliations. We aim to embed this in all that we do; in classrooms and curriculum, in workshops and events, and in 1:1 and group interactions.

name: Media & Entertainment Club
description: The Media & Entertainment Club (M&EC) at the Tepper School of Business welcomes all Carnegie Mellon University students to explore and engage with the work and art of the media and entertainment industries. We are a professional club that takes a holistic approach by providing career discovery, media appreciation, and entertainment-focused programming. We are also committed to building an inclusive community that brings people together through a shared passion for media and entertainment, while supporting students’ personal and professional growth and fostering connections across Tepper and th

name: Mellon FIT
description: The mission of Mellon Fit is to provide opportunities that promote health, fitness, and productivity to students and faculty in and around Mellon Institute while facilitating cross-disciplinary interaction and communication between neighboring departments.

name: Men's Club Volleyball
description: Carnegie Mellon Club Volleyball Team's mission is to give its members the opportunity to build teamwork and leadership skills through the game of volleyball. This organization strives to attain a high level of athletic success while maintaining the highest standard of sportsmanship, integrity, and team unity.

name: Men's Ultimate Frisbee Club
description: We aim to create a cohesive, fun, and competitive community around the sport of ultimate at CMU.

name: Men's Water Polo Club
description: Carnegie Mellon Men's Club Water Polo focuses on our members developing to become stronger water polo players, the team bonding and becoming more tight-knit through social gatherings, and on creating a competitive team to have success in tournaments. We compete in the Mid-Atlantic division of the Collegiate Water Polo Association and participate in tournaments throughout the fall and spring semesters. We have performed very well in last year's tournaments.

name: Middle Eastern and North African Student Association
description: With open arms and an inclusive spirit, MENASA encompasses a wider spectrum of cultures and traditions, uniting students from various Middle Eastern and North African countries. Our club reflects the rich culture of our region, embracing those who share our heritage. In MENASA, diversity of tongues is celebrated. Whether you're fluent in Arabic, speak another MENA language, or don't speak any at all, you are warmly welcomed to join our vibrant community. Come and be a part of this exciting journey to learn more about the Middle Eastern and North African student community.

name: Mock Trial
description: CMU Mock Trial aims to better educate its members about the U.S. legal system and trial advocacy. Members gain opportunities to travel, participate in collegiate mock trial tournaments, and compete in the regional competition.

name: Moneythink CMU
description: Moneythink CMU turns financial knowledge into action—empowering college mentors to build the financial capability of local youth while expanding opportunity across CMU and the Pittsburgh community. We work toward a future where everyone has the knowledge and confidence to take control of their financial future.

name: Mortarboard
description: Mortar Board, a national honor society that recognizes college seniors for their achievements in scholarship, leadership and service, provides opportunities for continued leadership development, promotes service to colleges and universities and encourages lifelong contributions to the global community.

name: Multicultural Greek Council
description: The Multicultural Greek Council at Carnegie Mellon University provides formal recognition and representation for its culturally based fraternities and sororities while serving as both a supportive and legislative body. Grounded in multiculturalism, MGC values diversity in all its forms and creates a platform for members to voice their perspectives and be heard. The Council fosters unity within the Greek community, promotes cultural awareness, encourages scholastic achievement, and ensures cooperation, accountability, and harmony among its member organizations.

name: Music Production Club
description: We seek to foster a vibrant music production community on campus, providing a platform for music producers and enthusiasts of all skill levels and genres to come together. Whether you're a beginner eager to dive into the world of music production or an experienced producer seeking like-minded individuals, our club is your sonic producer haven. We strive to create an inclusive space where members can learn, discuss, and share ideas on diverse facets of music production, including software, hardware, musical concepts, and production techniques. No genre is off-limits, and no digital audio workst

name: Muslim Student Association
description: The Muslim Student Association at CMU strives to address the religious, cultural, and social needs of Muslim students, and to build awareness and familiarity with Islam, Islamic cultures, and Muslims through positive interactions with the broader CMU community.

name: National Organization of Minority Architects Students
description: The National Organization of Minority Architects (NOMA) mission is to champion diversity within the design professions by promoting the excellence, community engagement, and professional development of its members. It is important to emphasize not only diversity of appearance, but also diversity of thoughts, views, and opinions.

name: National Society of Black Engineers
description: Founded in 1979 and chartered in 1980, NSBE's mission is "to increase the number of culturally responsible Black Engineers who excel academically, succeed professionally and positively impact the community."

name: National Society of Black Engineers - Healthcare Innovation Special Interest Group Chapter
description: CMU NSBE HISIG mission to support, promote, and develop Black engineers, scientists, and entrepreneurs as they create culturally responsible and racially equitable innovations in healthcare, medicine, biotechnology, and allied fields.

name: Panhellenic Council
description: The National Panhellenic Conference (NPC) is the premier advocacy and support organization for the advancement of the sorority experience. NPC was established in 1902 to assist collegiate and alumnae chapters of the NPC member organizations in cooperating with colleges and universities and to foster interfraternal relationships. We are committed to relationships built on trust through transparency, accountability and mutual respect. Innovation and our core values of friendship, leadership, service, knowledge, integrity and community guide us in fulfilling our mission.

name: Partners in Speculative Fiction
description: Partners in Speculative Fiction Book Club seeks to explore different stories, novels, and genres through weekly meetings. This club analyzes a variety of speculative fiction works and holds open discussions through on-campus gatherings.

name: Pi Tau Sigma
description: Pi Tau Sigma is the International Mechanical Engineering Honors Society. Our mission is to recognize superior scholarship, provide networking and career opportunities, and encourage kinship within the Mechanical Engineering Community.

name: Pickled Arts
description: Pickled Arts is a space for students of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences to come together and make art. Every student across Carnegie Mellon University is welcome to explore artistic practices in a low-stakes environment and join a creative community of student artists.

name: Pittsburgh Connections
description: Pittsburgh Connections engages students in outdoor recreation, environmental stewardship, and cultural awareness throughout Pittsburgh and Western Pennsylvania, with the goals to help students develop and maintain a physically active lifestyle, build leadership skills, and increase their appreciation of the region. Throughout the academic year, Pittsburgh Connections sponsors outdoor and cultural adventures to one of the many outdoor recreation facilities in the Pittsburgh area. Past adventure trips include whitewater rafting, kayaking, biking, hiking, paintball, horseback riding, and skiing!

name: Pittsburgh Go Association
description: The Pittsburgh Go Association is a go club located in Pittsburgh, PA dedicated to promoting the game of go (baduk, igo, weiqi) in the form of tournaments, rankings, and educational opportunities.

name: Pre-College Programs
description: Carnegie Mellon’s Pre-College Programs mirror the undergraduate experience, giving rising high school juniors and seniors the opportunity to explore their interests and passions while receiving instruction from acclaimed Carnegie Mellon faculty and staff. We provide a holistic and robust student experience that includes academic and personal development both inside and outside of the classroom to prepare students for the future.

name: Pre-Law Society
description: Our mission is to connect undergraduate students at Carnegie Mellon to resources and opportunities in the legal world that may be of benefit to them, as well as provide a community for students interested in attending law school after CMU.

name: PRISM
description: PRISM is a social and activist organization at Carnegie Mellon University for those of all genders and orientations. We provide a safe space for anyone with an open mind to find new friends, talk about issues, and raise awareness.

name: Product @ CMU
description: To build a community and support system for CMU students and alumni in product management, without barriers of majors and year.

name: Product Lab
description: It shall be the purpose of this organization to help students foster Product Management skills by working on projects with participating clients, including but not limited to Startups, Research Institutes, Corporate, Non-Government, and Non-Profit organizations.

name: Project Ignite
description: To utilize project based learning to expose high school students to subject areas that they would otherwise be unable to explore, and to enable high school students to pursue a new or existing interest that they lack the knowledge, resources, or support to engage in on their own, thus helping them develop passions that can be pursued at a professional level.

name: Project Smile
description: Our mission is to improve the overall well being and happiness of the student body through various acts of kindness motivated by scientific research.

name: Puzzlehunt CMU
description: Puzzle Hunt CMU is an interest group in all things related to puzzle hunts on and around the CMU campus. We have weekly meetings to discuss, write, and solve puzzles. We also run a puzzle hunt every semester. If you join us at our writing meetings, then you can contribute your own puzzles to the upcoming hunt, or you can playtest other people's puzzles. By coming to writing meetings, you will be helping us organize the upcoming hunt. If you want to play in the hunt, then stay tuned for posters around campus and a date on our website https://puzzlehunt.club.cc.cmu.edu/. Our fall hunt is around

name: Quant
description: The Quant Club of Carnegie Mellon University focuses on the study of quantitative finance, more specifically areas in finance where the study of mathematics and other computational aspects are emphasized.

name: Quiz Bowl
description: The purpose of CMU Quiz Bowl is to encourage participation in Quiz Bowl among students and those in the Pittsburgh region.

name: Recreational Volleyball Club
description: The mission of this club is to provide a space for members of the CMU community to play volleyball and improve the level of play for anyone and everyone who wants to play the game. All activities and functions of the organization must be legal under University, local, state, and federal laws.

name: Redeemed Campus Fellowship
description: Our mission is to build a community of fearless young people grounded in the principles of the Kingdom of God. We aim to cultivate loving, bold, and Holy Spirit-led leaders who live lives of light, shaped by the transformative power of God’s word. We welcome all students—regardless of background or belief—who are interested in exploring faith, engaging in meaningful community, and growing in purpose and leadership.

name: ReFlexion
description: As one of the few acapella groups dedicated to community outreach at CMU, ReFlexion’s goal is to spread our love of music not only to people on campus, but also to the surrounding Pittsburgh areas by performing at senior centers, children’s hospitals, and nearby schools. Our music covers a wide variety of genres, inspired by our group’s diverse music tastes, and we hope to inspire and spread positivity through our performances.

name: School of Music Student Advisory Board
description: The School of Music Student Advisory Board is a group of students committed to improving the community and experience within the Music School. We hear student's ideas and concerns and take on projects to better the school.

name: Scotch'n'Soda Theatre
description: As one of the nation's oldest student theatre organizations, Carnegie Mellon University's Scotch'n'Soda Theatre is an entirely student-run group dedicated to the development of theatrical works and educating the campus community on all aspects of theatre. Scotch'n'Soda is an interdisciplinary organization that values a versatile and diverse constituency devoted to creating unique, innovative, and entertaining products.
