name: Scottie Ventures
description: Scottie Ventures' mission is to introduce Carnegie Mellon students to the world of venture capital and private equity by giving them the opportunity to develop their skills, knowledge, and network needed to be successful in the industry.

name: Scotty Survivor
description: Scotty Survivor is an organization that provides students the opportunity to play and/or produce a collegiate version of CBS Survivor. We aim to be a social club that connects students from all different years and majors, while allowing them to compete in physical and mental challenges.

name: ScottyCon
description: ScottyCon is a student organization dedicated to planning and running ScottyCon, an annual anime and gaming convention catered to CMU and the greater Pittsburgh community. ScottyCon aims to connect the different subcultures of CMU by creating a collaborative event between different clubs at CMU. ScottyCon strives to continuously grow with its collaborations and integrate various organizations with each iteration. Visit our website for more info: https://www.scottycon.com/

name: ScottyLabs
description: We’re a student-run organization dedicated to building tech that enhances campus life—empowering the Carnegie Mellon University community to create, collaborate, and solve real-world problems through apps and events.

name: SEED Leadership Program
description: The mission of the SEED (Sustainability Education + Empowerment = Doing) Leadership program is to build a network of sustainability-literate student leaders capable of empowering and educating peers about sustainability issues.

name: Shotokan Karate Club
description: The mission of CMU Shotokan Karate is to provide training opportunities for students learning karate-do. Karate is a martial art, or fighting method, involving a variety of techniques, including blocks, strikes, evasions, throws, and joint manipulations. The word karate is a combination of two Japanese characters: kara, meaning empty, and te, meaning hand. Thus, karate means "empty hand." Adding the suffix "-do", meaning "way," i.e., karate-do, implies karate as a total way of life that goes well beyond the self-defense applications. name: Sigma Eta Pi
description: To provide real-world experience to budding entrepreneurs through education and social opportunities that will foster the next generation of entrepreneurs at CMU and provide lifelong connections to members.

name: Sikh Student Organization
description: The Sikh Student Association seeks to create a community to connect Sikh students at Carnegie Mellon University

name: Singapore Students' Association
description: The Singapore Students' Association at Carnegie Mellon University is a student organization dedicated to fostering an understanding of Singapore culture among the CMU community, as well as promoting interaction among its members. It also serves as a support network for incoming Singaporean students.

name: Ski & Snowboard Club
description: To provide students the opportunity to ski and snowboard during the season while at CMU, and to provide students with a community of those who also share their love for skiing/snowboarding.

name: SKY@CMU - Meditation Club
description: Bringing meditation, breathwork, emotional intelligence, social connection, and service leadership to college students, faculty and staff. National Chapter: https://www.skycampushappiness.org/about

name: Smart Woman Securities
description: Smart Woman Securities is a non-profit organization dedicated to educating women about the world of finance. We accomplish this task through instructive seminars, mentoring initiatives, and meetings with successful investors such as Warren Buffett. SWS is one of the few female-only investment organizations featuring undergraduate women in the United States. Our mission is to endow every woman with the proper skills and training in order to successfully invest on her own. Currently, there are 25 chapters operating at various universities in the United States. At our chapter, we have taken the i

name: Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics Student Chapter
description: A student chapter of the international professional organization SIAM, that is focused on current mathematical research and its applications. The SIAM student chapter hosts seminars and working groups to provide an opportunity for students to learn more about a variety of topics on applied mathematics.

name: Society of Asian Scientists and Engineers
description: SASE is dedicated to the advancement of Asian heritage scientists and engineers in education and employment so that they can achieve their full career potential. In addition to professional development, SASE also encourages members to contribute to the enhancement of the communities in which they live. Our mission is to: Prepare Asian heritage scientists and engineers for success in the global business world. Celebrate diversity on campuses and in the workplace. Provide opportunities for members to make contributions to their local communities. SASE membership is open to men and women of all e

name: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers
description: SHPE CMU empowers the Latinx community at CMU and the university community by providing academic, professional, social, and community outreach events which help our members grow and connect. We are more than just our Latinx or STEM affiliations, so we encourage inclusion and collaborations with other organizations and search for ways to grow the voices of our members.

name: Society of Physics Students
description: The Society of Physics Students (SPS) aims to engage all members of the Carnegie Mellon University Physics Department through weekly meetings and physics-themed events. It particularly focuses on undergraduate physics majors, promoting excitement about physics as well as personal and professional growth. The organization’s activities offer opportunities to socialize and to learn more about the paths available to them as physics students. This organization is established as a local chapter of the National Society of Physics Students Chapter # 991 within Zone 7. This organization also manages th

name: Society of Women Engineers
description: To promote the image and success of women in STEM both internal and external to SWE by providing resources for personal and professional development and a community that advocates diversity and awareness.

name: Soundbytes
description: Formed in 1996, Soundbytes is a group that strives to put the smooth and sultry into their performances, whether it's singing together on a whim or competing on the big stage. Prioritizing vibes and musicality equally, they're a group of close friends who enjoy making music together. In 2023, they competed in Troy, NY for ICCA and brought back awards for best arrangement, best soloist, best choreography, and placed second.

name: Spikeball Club
description: Spikeball/roundnet is a fun, exciting recreational sport with a devoted and passionate community. Our goal is to create a friendly and welcoming space for spikeball enthusiasts of all skill levels to enjoy the wonderful sport.

name: SPIRIT
description: To serve as a haven for Black students of diverse ethnic backgrounds and their allies within the Carnegie Mellon community, to serve as a two-way platform for the SPIRIT constituency and Carnegie Mellon community, and to champion the issues and awareness of the Black community and all its intersections.

name: Sports Marketing Club
description: Our mission is to empower students to turn their passion for sports marketing into careers through learning, networking, and real-world experience.

name: Spring Carnival Committee
description: To plan an awesome, enjoyable, inclusive, and safe Carnival experience for CMU students, alumni, and the entire Tartan community.

name: Steel City Shershaah
description: The purpose of this organization is to develop and promote a space of artistic and creative growth for South Asian performance, education, and civic engagement. Steel City Shershaah aims to diversify dance with a variety of dance styles including Bollywood, Bhangra, Hip-Hop, etc; and to share South Asian culture.

name: Steel Syncopation
description: The Steel Syncopation is an organization committed to celebrating and performing tap dance. Our mission is to welcome students of all backgrounds and levels to start or continue their learning of tap dance and be able to express their creativity through rhythm. This organization hopes to teach the community how to tap dance and increase the awareness of tap dance. This club aims to create a community of tappers who can come together to perform. This organization hopes to be a stress relief for CMU students, by providing a mentally stimulating and satisfying physical activity. Moreover, we hope

name: Stock Talks
description: Stock Talks is a discussion platform for the conversation and analysis of the stock market. Stock Talks aims to open discussion of the stock market to the community, while teaching students how to use their interests and skills in searching for internships and full-time work.

name: Strong Women Strong Girls
description: Our mission is to empower girls to imagine a broader future through a curriculum grounded on female role models. Our core values are accountability, quality, respect, community, and discovery. As a college chapter, we hope to make an impact on our local Pittsburgh community through mentoring, while also empowering and supporting our college mentors.

name: Student College
description: The Student College was established in 2001 to provide Carnegie Mellon students with the opportunity to share knowledge through educational, self-designed courses. Students can teach classes on any topic of their choice. However, the course cannot be available through regular University offerings. Courses typically meet once a week (for a full semester) and follow the current Carnegie Mellon academic calendar.

name: Student Dormitory Council (SDC)
description: The Student Dormitory Council (SDC) aims to improve the lives of residents at CMU by providing opportunities for residents to participate in events and activities through SDC, learn about residents around campus, and receive funding for their own events!

name: Student Government Director of Finance & JFC
description: The Student Government Director of Finance oversees the student activities fee including the allocation of funds to student organizations at Carnegie Mellon. They advocate for student organizations on financial matters, answer questions and problem solve related to the use of activities fee money, and oversee the process used to distribute and reconcile fees each year. The Joint Funding Committee (JFC) is the body that supports the budget request and allocation processes.

name: Student Government Director of Organizations & CoSO
description: The Student Government Director of Organizations oversees and advocates for student organizations at Carnegie Mellon. They direct the recognition of new organizations, re-recognition of existing organizations, and allocation/management of campus space for student organizations. The Committee on Student Organizations (CoSO) and University Center Allocation Board (UCAB) are the bodies that support these processes.

name: Student Government Executive Branch
description: The Carnegie Mellon Student Government consists of many groups, at their core governed by the Student Body Constitution. The Legislative branch consists of the Undergraduate Student Senate and the Graduate Student Assembly. The Executive branch consists of undergraduate and graduate students who work with campus advocacy, student organizations, and student finances. The Activities Board (AB) is an external committee that provides events, concerts, films, lectures, technical assistance, and other activities for the campus. name: Students Using Data for Social-Good
description: We aim to connect socially conscious students from all CMU schools to non-profits where they can apply their technical and communication skills to meaningful data management and analysis projects.

name: Sustainable Earth
description: Sustainable Earth aims to encourage Carnegie Mellon University and the Pittsburgh Community to actively practice ways of living sustainably.

name: Sweepstakes
description: Sweepstakes is responsible for the organizing, conducting, and supervising all activities related to the Sweepstakes (Buggy) competitions.

name: Taiwanese Scholar Society
description: Help incoming Taiwanese students to adapt to life in the US. Connect the Taiwanese community at CMU. Promote Taiwanese culture and community to CMU.

name: Taiwanese Students Association
description: The Taiwanese Students Association at Carnegie Mellon University is an organization that serves to bring cultural awareness, provide service to the community, and create social events throughout the CMU community via cultural, philanthropic, and social events. name: Tartan Athlete Fellowship
description: The Carnegie Mellon Tartan Athlete Fellowship is a student group looking to explore the role athletics play in our Christian faith and how our Christian faith affects the way we compete, play and live. This group uses athletics to facilitate discussions, but not everything is focused on sports. Everyone is welcome to attend, athlete and non-athlete alike. Come check us out if you're interested in being part of a group exploring faith, college, sports and living. Tartan Athlete Fellowship is a ministry of the CCO. Insta: @ccotaf

name: Tartan Cycling
description: Tartan Cycling is established to provide a framework for existing CMU cyclists to connect, as well as a mechanism to introduce interested students to the sport of cycling. We hold group meetings to provide relevant information to new members, organize cycling events accessible to all skill levels, and give students interested in collegiate racing the opportunity to participate.

name: Tartan Links Golf Club
description: Tartan Links is a golf club dedicated to making golf more accessible and affordable for all students at Carnegie Mellon University. Our mission is to lower the barriers to the sport by providing clubs, organizing rides to local golf courses, and creating opportunities for students of all skill levels to play and learn together. Whether you are an experienced golfer or trying the game for the first time, Tartan Links provides the support and community to help you get involved. More than just a golf club, Tartan Links is also a social and professional network. Our name reflects both our connecti

name: Tartan Marketing Association
description: The American Marketing Association at CMU aims to provide opportunities for students to: - Participate in hands-on projects to gain technical and soft skills - Network with professionals and explore possible careers in the marketing and business fields - Develop interests in marketing and the American Marketing Association

name: Tartan NeuroTech
description: Our mission is to engage more students in different areas of study in the field of neurotechnology, more specifically, Brain/Muscle-Computer Interfaces. We achieve our mission through giving student-led intro lectures, organizing industrial talks, and leading hackathon group projects.

name: TepperCARES
description: TepperCares leads community service initiatives in the Greater Pittsburgh Area. Our goal is to provide volunteers with high-quality service experiences that complement the MBA education.

name: THE FAIR
description: The FAIR showcases many of CMU's 300+ Student Government recognized student organizations, 23 sorority and fraternity organizations, and partners from around campus and the Pittsburgh community. The entire CMU community - undergraduate and graduate students, staff, and faculty - are invited to explore ways to get involved at Carnegie Mellon and beyond.

name: The Flying Club
description: The Flying Club at Carnegie Mellon University is a platform to promote flying and aviation at Carnegie Mellon University and the Greater Pittsburgh area. It is intended to be a space at Carnegie Mellon University where those interested in flying and aviation can congregate, share experiences, promote flying, and help others reach their goals in aviation and flying.

name: The Frame
description: The Frame is a non-profit, student-run art space. We are committed to showcasing the artistic work of Carnegie Mellon students and to promoting ambitious and experimental art within our community, campus and Pittsburgh.

name: The Oakland Review
description: To publish a literary journal based in the Carnegie Mellon campus community. To cultivate an appreciation and enthusiasm for literature and art in the Carnegie Mellon community.

name: The Originals
description: The purpose of The Originals is to advance musicianship, foster creative expression and push the boundaries of a cappella, both internally, and in the Carnegie Mellon University campus at large.

name: The Tartan
description: The Tartan is a student-run weekly newspaper serving the Carnegie Mellon University community, a student organization dedicated to informing students about affairs and opinions relevant to them, and a forum for opinions from the university community. Members of The Tartan meet weekly on Mondays in UC 314 at 5 p.m. to discuss content for the upcoming week for our various sections, including News, Forum, SciTech, Sports, and Pillbox (The Tartan's Art & Culture magazine). name: The Treblemakers
description: The mission of The Treblemakers is to provide a supportive community for students with a passion for singing and a cappella.

name: The Writing Academy
description: To create a place at CMU for writers to pursue professional and creative interest

name: Theme Park Engineering Group
description: Our organization's mission is to connect people to the themed entertainment industry through opportunities to hear from industry professionals, go to the parks, and network with people that are already involved in the industry. Some overall objectives are to cultivate a community of people that are passionate about themed entertainment, seek university support for people to go to industry conventions, and encourage involvement in industry competitions.

name: Turkish Student Society
description: It aims to promote Turkish Culture on Campus and in Pittsburgh, to help new students to adapt the life in Pittsburgh, and to improve the connections between Turkish CMU Alumni and CMU students for networking purposes.

name: Undergraduate Consulting Club
description: We strive to expand the horizons and the possibilities of what our school and our students can do in the consulting world. We provide the necessary tools to support our members in their journey towards a fascinating career in the consulting industry.

name: Undergraduate Entrepreneurship Association
description: CMU Undergrad Entrepreneurship Association is a rapidly growing and inclusive club that fosters a community of aspiring entrepreneurs. Our mission is to provide a platform for students to develop their entrepreneurial skills, connect with industry professionals, and create meaningful relationships with like-minded individuals. We empower our members through a diverse range of events, such as workshops, speaker events, networking opportunities, and competitions.

name: Undergraduate Student Senate
description: The Carnegie Mellon Undergraduate Student Senate is the undergraduate component of Carnegie Mellon's Student Government Legislative Branch. We are composed of student-elected representatives that represent the unique and diverse culture of our university. Elected representatives from each Carnegie Mellon college meet on a weekly basis to discuss rising issues on our campus. Our general body meetings are every Thursday at 5:00p EST, and are open to everyone in the Carnegie Mellon community. For the 2022-23 school year, GBMs will be held in the Cohon Center Danforth Conference Room.

name: Underground Writer's Society
description: The mission of Underground Writer’s Society is to foster the development of individual writing projects and work with peers to improve story ideas and writing.

name: University Rowing Club
description: CMU's Rowing Team was founded in 1989, and has since become the largest Club sport at Carnegie Mellon. Committed to teamwork, athleticism, and academic excellence, Tartan Crew continues to create an all-inclusive environment for dedicated Student-Athletes.

name: User Experience Student Association
description: UXA mission is to support our members confidence and self-actualization in practicing HCI through fulfilling three fundamental pillars: foster social engagement; provide support for academic success; and accelerate career readiness.

name: Vermillion Anime Club
description: Our mission at Vermillion Anime Club is to foster interest in Japanese anime and manga, and to provide a community for individuals that hold such interests.

name: Vietnamese Student Association
description: Our mission as VSA is to promote, preserve, and advocate for the Vietnamese and Vietnamese-American culture. We also hope to aid the growth and development of the Carnegie Mellon University collegiate students through the creation of cultural, advocacy, academic, and community-focused events about the Vietnamese and Vietnamese-American culture.

name: Wellness and Meaning-Making Programs
description: The Office of Wellness and Meaning-Making Programs is comprised of Wellness Initiatives and Religious and Spiritual Life. Staff in this department work in partnership with campus and community resources to offer a wide array of workshops, personal development opportunities, community-connection events, and services to support students' holistic health. name: Wilton E. Scott Institute for Energy Innovation
description: We address the world’s most pressing energy challenges by enabling collaborative research, strategic partnerships, policy outreach, entrepreneurship, and education. We support impactful work that strives to optimize resources and reduce environmental consequences associated with energy production and use. We understand that energy and social equity issues are deeply interconnected, and society can benefit from improved energy access. We seek to encourage the development of breakthrough technologies that will accelerate the transition to a sustainable, net-zero energy future.

name: Women in Biomedical Engineering
description: The mission of CMU Women in BME is to bring knowledge, networking opportunities, and mentorship to women in Biomedical Engineering (BME). Our efforts are aimed at closing the gender gap by increasing the number of women who i) enter the field, ii) pursue higher education, and iii) obtain positions of elevated rank within companies and universities. Our organization is open to individuals of all genders. Members include graduate students, individuals working in industry, and professors interested in discussing the impact of gender in BME and closely-related disciplines.

name: Women in Business
description: Women in Business is an undergraduate organization focused on empowering women in the workplace through raising awareness about gender equity and professional development. We serve to help young women in college navigate the professional field and develop personal connections throughout the community.

name: Women in CyberSecurity
description: WiCyS is where the recruitment, retention and advancement of women in cybersecurity happens. We welcome members of all genders and colleges/programs - as long as you have an interest in cybersecurity, you are welcome here!

name: Women in International Security
description: The mission of CMU WIIS is to elevate the voices of women in the field of international security, and to promote discourse and broaden perspectives regarding the role gender plays in international security through conversations and outreach between students, faculty, and community members.

name: Women in MechE
description: Empowering female engineers who strive to better the world around them while creating a supportive community among students here at CMU. Any member of the Carnegie Mellon University community with interest in the mission and goals of Women in MechE may become a member of the organization. Membership shall not be denied to any person because of age, race, gender, disability, sexual orientation, religion, familial status, or national origin.

name: Women in Product
description: Women in Product is a student organization focused on empowering women in product management through mentorship, hands-on workshops, and peer support. Membership is open to any member of the Carnegie Mellon University community who is interested in the mission and goals of our organization.

name: Women in Science
description: We are the Women in Science Club! We welcome people of any gender, major, and college into our organization. Our club's objective to promote a strong community of support, service, and education between women, other gender minorities, and their peers. We strive to form connections between classes and majors and give women access to mentors and role models within academia and industry. We aim to create a strong community of support for gender minorities in science to navigate our current and future careers through community service, education, professional development, and social events.

name: Women's Club Basketball
description: Our mission is to create an environment for women to compete against each other and play competitive basketball against other schools, while promoting teamwork, sportsmanship, and community.

name: Women's Club Lacrosse
description: Join a community of supportive and energetic women who enjoy the sport of lacrosse. Whether you've played for several years, or you're new to the sport, everyone is welcome and guaranteed to grow while still having fun.

name: Women's Club Soccer
description: CMU's Women's Club Soccer team aims to provide women of Carnegie Mellon University an opportunity to play competitive intercollegiate soccer, and promote fitness, friendship, and teamwork!

name: Women's Club Volleyball
description: Our mission an organization is to provide a fun and safe space for all women to play volleyball at a competitive yet manageable level.

name: Women's Self Defense
description: Our club is dedicated to teaching students the skills needed to effectively protect themselves in situations where they lack a physical advantage. Our aim is to provide students with a foundational understanding of hand-to-hand combat, weapon familiarity, and techniques for defusing hazardous scenarios. Moreover, we'll instruct you on utilizing everyday household items, such as water bottles and umbrellas, as defensive tools in the event of an attack. name: Women's Ultimate Frisbee Club
description: We are the Money Mellons, CMU's Women's Ultimate Frisbee Club. Our focus is to introduce new players to the sport, as well as advance the growth of skilled players: all levels of experience are welcome (in fact, the majority of players start ultimate in college)! We strive to create a community for people who want to form lifelong friendships and memories and focus on fostering a fun atmosphere that is competitive come game-time. name: Women's Water Polo
description: Women's Water Polo welcomes players of all skill levels and abilities to enjoy the game of water polo. We strive to create a team atmosphere that is fun and supportive, but also competitive during games. Throughout the year, we practice three days a week and compete with other collegiate water polo teams in the region.

name: WRCT 88.3FM
description: As a free-form radio broadcaster, we are committed to providing quality alternatives to the mainstream commercial programming that dominates the radio. Our DJs, Public Affairs hosts, and other staff members are not only Carnegie Mellon students, staff, and faculty, but also community members from the Pittsburgh area, some of whom have more than 30 years of radio broadcasting experience under their belts. name: Yarnivores
description: Founded in 2012, Yarnivores is an organization that allows knitters and crocheters on campus to meet and discuss projects or learn new skills. We teach yarn crafts, facilitate charitable crafting, and organize yarn crafting events on campus.

name: Young African Leaders Association
description: Our mission is to create a community for the African diaspora on campus by giving a place to talk about and experience their diverse cultures. Furthermore, we hope to spread knowledge about this college to all members of the CMU campus in order to facilitate an environment of inclusion, curiosity and open mindedness.

name: Young Life College
description: Young Life College is all about building authentic community, walking through life together, and creating space to explore faith. Through weekly events, small groups, and trips, students are invited to grow in friendships and take their next steps in following Jesus. It’s a space for everyone — whether you’ve never heard of Jesus or have been walking with Him for a while.
